# Preface {.unnumbered}

## In this book {.unnumbered}

This book is designed for members of Biometrics departments in
biopharmaceutical companies who design, perform, review, or govern clinical
study reports and want to integrate AI systematically into their work.

After reading the Introduction, you will be able to:

- distinguish AI adoption for an isolated task from an AI-first workflow;
- state the five principles of trustworthy assistance and read a task
  contract;
- name the six AI-first SDLC stages, their canonical artifacts, and the human
  gate at each stage; and
- choose one bounded workflow in your own work that could become AI-first.

Familiarity with clinical study artifacts such as the protocol, statistical
analysis plan, and tables, listings, and figures will help you connect the
examples to your own work. No coding experience and no prior experience
building AI agents are required for the main route. The optional technical
route uses R and the exercise folders described on the landing page.

Each part of the book makes certain assumptions about the readers' background:

- Introduction, for shared concepts, principles, agent basics, and the AI-first SDLC.
- Applied examples, for bounded workflows developed through that lifecycle.
  The rounding example (Chapters 6--7) spans a motivating chapter and one
  lifecycle design; Chapter 8 is a companion lab built on the same skill.
  Later examples
  follow the same lifecycle at the maturity their evidence supports.
